messages:
Alex G: Quick idea I sketched this morning — a lightweight policy-translation gateway between the control plane and runtime adapters. Purpose: centralize 'intent' -> runtime config mapping so hosted/dedicated/private share one policy surface.

Maria C: Sounds promising. Can you sketch the boundaries? Is this another service in the control plane or a compile-time component? :thinking:

Alex G: Runtime-adjacent control-plane service. Not a full compiler. Think of it as a deterministic translator: take policy objects + route hints -> produce adapter-specific manifests (or delta patches). Keeps business intent stable while allowing adapter variations.

Shiv P: A couple tradeoffs: single translator = simpler for product, but becomes a coupling point for all deployments. Outage or bug affects everything. How do we handle fallbacks?

Alex G: Agreed. Plan is: (1) lightweight validation layer that rejects invalid translations, (2) per-tenant caches so adapter can continue if gateway is unreachable, (3) versioned translation rules and a safe rollback.

Diane L: And auth. Private deployments won't want translation rules flowing out. We need to support 'local-only' overrides and a safe sync model. Maybe rules can be pushed, but always sign and timestamp them.

Maria C: Also think about observability: we need token-level reasoning why a runtime got X config. Suggest we emit translation trace IDs and attach them to telemetry. That way Console can show "why a route was routed to variant B".

Shiv P: What about the API shape? I propose input schema: {intent: string, constraints: [...], routeHints: {...}, tenantId: string, desiredSLO: {...}} and output is either full adapter manifest or a patch + metadata. Example:

```json
{
  "intent": "low-latency-text-gen",
  "constraints": ["no-external-models"],
  "routeHints": {"region": "eu-west-1", "tier": "dedicated"},
  "tenantId": "acme-corp",
  "desiredSLO": {"p95_ms": 200}
}
```

ops-bot: translation-service deployed to canary (dc-eu-01) at 2498765440 :rocket:

Alex G: For adapters that need kv-caching or quantization flags, the gateway should emit capability flags and a small advisory block rather than hardcode low-level kernel settings. Adapter can choose to honour or fallback. Example output: `{manifest: {...}, capabilities: ["kv-cache"], advisory: "prefer-quant-int8"}`.

Diane L: That helps private deployments: they can run a local translator that consumes the same rule format but refuses rules flagged 'control-plane-only'. So the format should include explicit policy provenance and an allowlist.

Maria C: Rollouts: translation rules should support canary percentages and shadow deployments. Translation-service needs deterministic randomness seed so we can reproduce routing decisions for debugging.

Shiv P: Performance: keep translation quick (sub-ms for cached rules). Cold translation might involve policy graph evaluation. Idea: precompile common tenant profiles into adapter-ready bundles on commit.

Alex G: Security checklist: signed rules, audit trail, immutable rule versions, per-tenant KMS wrapping for private overrides. Diane — can you drive KMS + signing design?

Diane L: Yep, I'll draft a small RFC. Quick Q: do we want a per-tenant translator binary for air-gapped? Or a container image that can run locally and operate off signed rule bundles?

Alex G: Prefer container image with signed bundles push/pull. Keep control-plane orchestration minimal.

Maria C: One last nit: we should avoid the translator making resource placement decisions (GPU sizing etc.) — keep it at the config/flag level. Placement stays in the scheduler. Translator can emit placement hints, but not decide.

Alex G: Good call. I'll turn this into a short RFC: goals, API schema, lifecycle (authoring -> signing -> publish -> cache), and a risk matrix. Expect draft by EOD tomorrow.

Shiv P::+1: Looking forward. Will add perf guardrails to RFC.
